newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maturing May dominates slow Budapest grains market.
newsitem.headline: Maturing May dominates slow Budapest grains market.

text.p: Maturing May futures accounted for the bulk of turnover in the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), traders said on Wednesday.
"This week May prices showed rather hectic movements," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap.
May maize closed at 19,000 forints per tonne, up 300, after dropping 400 and 300 forints on Monday and Tuesday respectively.
May milling wheat moved in the opposite direction, easing 160 forints to 27,400 on the last day of trade after rising both on Monday and Tuesday.
The two May maturities accounted for 522 lots of a modest grains turnover of 1,206 contracts or 563.45 million forints, down from Tuesday's 1.09 billion.
August milling wheat, the only other maturity with a considerable turnover, rose 340 forints to 24,640 and Uzonyi said it was the preferred maturity for speculation.
"Open contracts for August equal the number of those for all other (wheat) maturities put together," he said.
There are 5,200 open contracts for August milling wheat.
Due to May Day public holidays, the next market day in Hungary will be Monday, May 5.
